utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody around the court. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we please have the appearances for today starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours; good morning to my colleagues from the Prosecution. I am Vasvija Vidovic representing General Delic, with assistants Lana Deljkic and Sabina Dzubur, and assisted by league assistant of OKO, Ms. Nina Kisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Awad. I know you do know this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I know you do know this, but it's still my duty to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic. Oh, your colleague is on his feet. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just very briefly. I wanted to put on the record the document Exhibit 67, or the document marked for identification as number 67, which was the list that was discussed at length with the witness yesterday, our records from the Prosecution side indicate that that document was previously marked for identification but not admitted. We've been -- because we're sitting here without access to all of the databases in The Hague, the registrar was also unable to confirm if that document had actually been admitted or simply marked. At this point, the Prosecution position is that that document clearly should be admitted into evidence if it has not previously been admitted into evidence, and I wanted to put that on the record here before it gets lost in the shuffle or we discover when we return to The Hague that it actually wasn't admitted. So our -- I simply want to put on the record the Prosecution position in light of -- especially in light of the extensive evidence concerning that document. We believe that document should be admitted if it hasn't been previously. And again, that was the document either Exhibit 67 or the document marked for identification as number 67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic, do you have anything to say on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The witness commented on that document. It's the list that we looked at yesterday. I do not believe that that document can be admitted through this witness. The witness actually said that the document does not reflect the actual situation. He mentioned the people who are referred to there, said that they didn't know each other, and if the document has been marked for identification, I believe that it should remain as such. So there were not enough elements for the document to be admitted into evidence. The reason why I showed the document to the witness is that at the -- some point I asked to look at the original of the document, and I contested the authenticity of the document. I apologise for not having in my records here that it's a MFI document, because when you print the report, then that column indicating the status of MFI documents is not actually shown in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I have a little bit of a problem with your objection, and I'd like you to clarify me here. You say that you asked the witness extensively about a document, and he said it doesn't show the correct position. Is -- is there a criterion for admission for -- because, in fact, many documents will be admitted because they've been properly identified, but whether or not they are telling the correct position is a different matter. We never know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, you're correct, but the witness did not identify the document and that's the point. He didn't identify it or accepted it as something that is -- he's familiar with in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's a new point you are making.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, it does seem as if we're in a bind about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the issues are clearly articulated by the Defence as to why she's objecting, but certainly it would be our view that this document has been testified about from the witness. He's identified his own name on the document and a number of other individuals whose names are on the document. I believe in the total context of all the evidence heard the Trial Chamber will be in a proper position to give the document whatever weight it might deem appropriate, but certainly the factors that the Defence have identified are not necessarily factors that would about against admitting the document, and so our position would be that the document, in light of the totality of the evidence the Chamber has heard and will hear in the future, that the document certainly is admissible at this stage of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to ask the parties to -- to make submissions on the point that I'm going to ask. This is the last witness for the Prosecution, and let us assume that this document is not admitted and the Defence doesn't call any witness to whom this document could be admitted. What becomes the value of the testimony that we have heard about this document? I'd like to hear you on that one, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's very simple. It will not be an exhibit in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The question was what becomes of the testimony that the witness has given in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can clarify that. What -- the testimony will stay in the transcript, because at this point the Defence cannot know if the Prosecutor will or will not show that document to any of the Defence witnesses. The Defence believes that this witness is someone who can identify or not identify this document and can speak -- about who can speak about the document, and that's the reason the Defence used it. So we would like to keep the explanation that the witness provided on the transcript, because at this point we cannot know what will be happening in the future when we bring before you our some 20 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Certainly the Prosecution would conquer with the Defence on that limited point. Obviously any oral evidence that the Chamber's had would remain on the record, on the transcripts, and would certainly be matters for the Trial Chamber to consider. Let me just add with respect to this document that we've had numerous documents shown to witnesses during the course of this trial. Witnesses have simply identified names on the document, and that alone has served as a foundation for the admission of documents, and this document is no different in that respect. And again, given the totality of the evidence, the Chamber will certainly be in a position to give this document whatever weight, if any, it deems necessary at the completion of all of the evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The exhibit will still remain as -- as marked for identification at this stage. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ajman, you testified over these couple of days about the relationship between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the commands of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I would like to clarify the relationship between the detachment and the higher commands of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I will remind you that on the first day of your testimony, you talked about a meeting with General Mehmed Alagic at the IKM of the Bosanska Krajina OG Lupac in the autumn of 1993. You said that Wahiuddeen was present at the meeting. What I would like to ask you to clarify is the following: General Alagic did not issue any orders to Wahiuddeen at that time or issue any assignments to him. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. He did not issue any orders at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were simply trying to agree how to continue the fighting?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, how to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yesterday I reminded you that you gave a statement to the Prosecutor in August and September 2005. Do you remember that you said in the statement that Alagic -- that "We were not very much to Alagic's liking"? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that the detachment did not receive Alagic's orders, but that Asim Koricic, whom you considered as a man of faith and a good Muslim, convinced the detachment command to go into actions precisely because you were not accepting Alagic's orders? Would this be a fair thing to say?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be fair to say that this was in one action that took place in late 1993. This was an action at Zabrdzje near Kruscica, that area towards Vitez. The detachment took part in it with the 7th Muslim Brigade. Maybe the 17th Krajina Brigade was also there in that action along that axis. All the coordination went through Asim Koricic, because the El Mujahedin Detachment command could trust him. We did not like to talk to Alagic all that much, because Alagic was a man who was a soldier with strict military -- and a strict military attitude. As far as he was concerned, we were undisciplined. And if you refuse one of his orders, he considered you undisciplined, lacking in discipline. He would issue orders as a commander, military orders, without discussion, without debate, and so on. We wouldn't accept that ever. First of all, we would discuss the terrain, the lay of the land, the options, and so on, not just go out as a soldier and get killed as a soldier without anybody asking about you. No. We would discuss first if it could or couldn't be done. So we didn't receive his direct orders in the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the OG Bosanska Krajina to which you were resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't understand which part of the testimony you didn't hear. What is it the last question and answer that there was no interpretation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Your question was not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It has, however, since been.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajman, I asked if at the time when you described this event Mr. Alagic, General Alagic, was the commander of the Operations Group Bosanska Krajina to which you were resubordinated at that time. When I say "you," I'm thinking of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the statement, I would like the witness to look at D788.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at page 2, and you will see paragraph 149 of your statement. It's not a long passage, and I'm going to quote it. In the conversation with the investigators, you said: "Until the establishment of the detachment we were not under the command, and even after the establishment of the detachment nobody could order anything to the El Mujahedin except for the emir of the Mujahedin." Do you remember saying that, Mr. Ajman?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, what you said is how it actually was, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need for excerpts from the statement to be entered into evidence so that we don't encumber the record with an unnecessary number of documents, so I won't ask for an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajman, the Prosecutor yesterday asked you on a number of occasions who set the priorities and the objectives of combat activities for the El Mujahedin Detachment, and you answered the corps. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to suggest to you the following: The corps did issue orders. However, whether those orders would be carried out or not was always a matter decided within the detachment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. I tried to explain clearly before any kind of action there would be a discussion. We would be told that such-and-such a terrain needed to be cleared, that this would be use if full, et cetera. And when we agreed to do something, then such an order would be issued to us in formal format. But if we didn't agree, then such an action or an attack would not be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Excuse me, Witness. Could you give us a precise example when you did the not launch an attack which had previously been decided by the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I spoke about that. This happened in 1994, when the El Mujahedin Detachment moved from the Sarici-Teslic front to the Zavidovici-Vozuca front, when we were required to attack three features, 726, 702, and 706, and we explained that the attack could not be carried out with success because of the nature of the terrain. And we didn't want to carry out that attack, but they insisted on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but yesterday, or perhaps the other day - I can no longer remember - when you spoke about this, my understanding was that nevertheless, there were negotiations, that you explained the reasons, and those reasons were acknowledged. So I did not understand that there was a confrontation over this particular decision and that you didn't obey it. That was not my understanding.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that the attack could not be carried out. However, they insisted, because other units were ready for it, and they were waiting for us, and we didn't launch the attack. But in order to fulfil some kind of a form so there wouldn't be any conflict between the corps command and the detachment command and others, I call this a fake attack, but it wasn't a real attack. When you fire from the existing lines, that is not an attack because there was no movement towards enemy lines. We were on the front line in trenches, and from the trenches we fired into the air -- or, rather, towards the enemy. So this wasn't a proper attack at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Having decided to launch a fake attack or false attack, in fact you didn't have the courage to directly oppose the decision.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could have done that if we had wanted to, but our -- the purpose of our stay there -- our coming there was not to clash with the Bosnian army or the Bosniaks. We had come to assist these people. So as to avoid a conflict, we did this something, fired a little bit, did some shooting just so that they could say something had been done.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is sufficient for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajman, let me ask you, in connection with what you have just said, a few brief questions. In such a situation that you have just described regarding the Ozren-Vozuca front, you were given a clear assignment to carry out an attack; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you didn't launch the attack. You just fired into the air; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't carry out the order to attack, not in the way you were ordered to do, nor at the time when you were order to attack. Am I right, in very simple terms?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That attack was not carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you didn't carry it out at the time that you were ordered to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I mean attack, I mean moving towards enemy lines. We didn't move at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no. But -- but what you call a fake, did that take place at the time that you were order to do so or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we had agreed that the attack be placed -- that the attack take place in the morning, we did what I have just described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, listen to my question. You have told us that you faked an attack. You're being asked -- okay. You faked the attack, and you did it at the time which was not the time you had ordered been -- you had been ordered to do it. I want to know whether this fake took place at the time other than the time ordered, or because of what you've explained, you didn't come here to clash, you came here to assist, you decided to go at the time when you -- you wanted -- you were ordered to go but you decided to fake it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time agreed. Maybe not the exact hour, but at the time agreed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this not the attack that you talked about either yesterday or the day before in which you said that there were no leaves, there was no foliage, is that the same attack? At that time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, at that time there was no foliage. It was a different season of the year. According to you, you wanted to do it in the season when there is foliage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did carry it out in the spring. The 27th of May, 1995, that is when we did carry out that attack, but not in November 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't follow your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me try and clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, you did not implement the order of the 3rd Corps with respect to the method nor with respect to the timing of that action, that is, in November 1994; is that right? I'm talking about the operation at the end of November 1994.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't follow the instructions regarding the method of carrying out the attack. The attack was intended against 726, 702, and 706, but actually there was an attack close to those features. Before those features, not at the features themselves. Fire was opened from existing lines, which cannot be identified with these features 702, 706, and 726.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also explained to us your participation in an operation in the region of Pisana Jelika and Visoko Glava. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the detachment received an order to take part in that operation together with some other units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some other units, I don't know whether it was the 7th or some others, that were supposed to attack together with the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, a decision was made within the detachment that the detachment act alone because it lacked confidence in the army units. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the order to the detachment to take part together with the other army units was not observed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me go back to what we were discussing a moment ago. Am I right -- or, rather, let me put the following to you: The detachment set its own conditions to a high level command for participation in an operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, a high level command, whether it was the division or the 3rd Corps, could not count on the detachment at a point in time when it felt the detachment was necessary or when it ordered that it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the conditions were fulfilled for an attack, we would never carry out an attack. Let me explain to make things quite clear. For instance, the terrain at Sarici is very difficult. It is very difficult to draw out or to carry out the wounded, and we insisted that a path had to be made, a road, and we used large machines to make a road there so that the jeeps could reach as close as possible to the area of attack for us to be able to save the wounded. Other units did not ask for this, but we insisted. We said there's -- we would not allow the operation to begin for our wounded to die there, whereas we can save them and take them to hospital if we have a road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, please don't think that I'm trying to prove that your reasons were not correct, the reasons for your actions, but I am simply trying to convey a fact. The command did give orders, but unlike other units, you did not observe those orders. You simply decided on your own whether you would accept an order or not. Would that be a fair summary of what you have said?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like the witness now to be shown P789 [sic], please. D, D789. 89. It is part of a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at paragraph 154 and the last sentence in it, and I'll quote it for you. It's not long. Judging by what you said to the investigator while talking to him: "The command would pressure us in order to prepare the action as soon as possible, but we would often meet their request somewhere in the middle based on the situation in the field." And what I wish to ask you now is the following: First of all, did you say this to the Prosecutor, and is that right? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this is the statement made on the 13th of September, 1995, and my signature is there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 2005. Correction, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what I said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what you said is true.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask in connection with the decision-making within the El Mujahedin Detachment. The detachment had an Shura; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a body that made decisions within the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were present at Shura meetings, because you would occasionally interpret to Bosniaks who participated in the work of the Shura; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present only at the meetings attended by Bosniaks, because the Shura was composed of Arabs and Bosniaks. Sometimes the Arabs would meet alone. Then I wouldn't attend. But when interpretation was necessary I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Bosniaks were present at the Shura were we will who were -- who headed the groups that went in -- that launched attacks, that actually led the El Mujahedin attacks?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually there were men who would lead these groups into attacks. And then, for instance, there would be a group of scouts who would carry out reconnaissance. So there was -- there was a group that would carry out the attack, but there were also scouts, and they were present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the Shura considered and discussed the plan of the attack, whether the attack would be carried out or not and so on. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition, the Shura decided on all the major issues concerning the life and work of the detachment. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point could the witness please be shown Exhibit 842. Exhibit 842, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 43.41 it have 819, you don't -- you're not asking for anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Exhibit 842 is a document from the El Mujahedin Detachment of 23rd October, 1993, and entitled "Shura Decision." The document is brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I'm sure you've had opportunity to read it now. It is about the meeting of the Shura on the 23rd of October, 1993, concerning some event involving a disciplinary infraction by El Mujahedin named Mujahid Sabahudin [phoen], where he was issued the last warning because he had done certain things without the unit's emir, and he was punished by being placed in detention. What I would like to ask you is this, Mr. Awad: This is a disciplinary decision issued by the Shura; is that correct? Is it correct that the Shura considered and dealt with discipline in this manner?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the meaning of the phrase "he had done certain things without the emir"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Emmer [as interpreted] [phoen]. Without an emmer. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What it means is that he did this without the permission of the emir. If somebody wanted to do something, he would have to do it with the permission of the emir. Without it, he would not be allowed to do it. In this particular case, this man, Sabahudin, had done something not within the detachment itself, within the camp or the command, but some -- at some other place without the knowledge of the emir, and as a consequence somebody complained of his behaviour, and then he was issued this warning and punished with detention for 15 days. And it was also stated that if anything similar happened in the future, he would not remain in the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to this, I would like to ask you this: It is true, isn't it, that the detachment had its internal orders which were not, in fact, the orders issued by the army of the -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The internal organisation of the El Mujahedin Detachment followed the code. In other words, it had nothing to do with the BH army code. We had our own code and certain rules that the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment had to abide by.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in that case what infraction was involved, if you know, in this particular case, please?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think this had something to do with the school. I think there was an issue with a schoolteacher, that there was some kind of conflict between them, and then she complained. Her complaint reached the unit commander, the detachment commander. So -- in other words, he went there and he said, "I'm a Mujahedin, and I can do anything." In other words, he posed as if he were a representative of the detachment and El Mujahedin. However, he did not have a permission -- the emir's permission for this. So perhaps this was the way he acted. He went there and said, "I'm a Mujahedin, so I can do this," whatever that was. And this he was not allowed to do. Whatever he did he could do in his own name, you but if he said that he was doing it in the name of the Mujahedin, he could not -- he was not allowed to do this. This was not the only such case. There were several instances where people were punished because of this kind of behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of an internal code of behaviour for members of the detachment. Did you also have a code that applied to relations with the 3rd Corps and the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have a written code. There was nothing written down. These were roles that applicable. This was the conduct of the people who were members of the detachment. And also the conduct towards the 3rd Corps or the 35th Division or any other unit, an operative group. There was Operative Group 3 North or Bosnian Krajina and the like.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Where did you detain this gentleman? Did you have a prison of your own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date on this document is 1993, which means that we didn't have any premises where somebody would be kept in detention, but I think he was just held in a room. So what I'm trying to say is that in 1993, we didn't have premises, detention premises. But after this, when at the command in Pobrezje in Zenica, there was a room which was known as room number 4, and this was used for detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point I wish to have the witness shown document D796. D796, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction: D766.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I would like to address an issue, but before that let me just say that this is a document of the security service of the 3rd Corps of 20th December 1995, and I would like to focus your attention on the first section, the first section of this document, the first paragraph, because I would like to put a question related to a fact that is stated there.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is about a decision issued by the Shura regarding the departure of the Mujahedin from Zenica. What I would like to ask you is this: Is it true that the Shura considered -- discussed this issue of the departure of the Mujahedin from Bosnia and that it was the Shura, in fact, who made this decision? In other words, that it accepted something that was proposed by the Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only was it discussed -- not only was this issue discussed, the departure of the Mujahedin, at the Shura, they also discussed whether the detachment should be disbanded or not. And regardless of the signing of the Dayton Accords, it was discussed whether the detachment should be disbanded and -- or whether we should, regardless of this, just continue with the fighting. The people who were in the Shura, and it was not just the corps Shura but a broader group of people, everyone was there, and they were all in favour because of the results that had already been accomplished by then in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In order to maintain the good relationship with the Bosnian people and in order to avoid a conflict, an internecine, a fight or war that we would have started, everyone decided that the detachment should be disbanded, and they expressed their readiness to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina. Had such a decision not been made, it is certain that the detachment would not have been disbanded and none of it would have happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Awad, regardless of the fact this the decision that was signed at the -- in Dayton, at the Dayton Accord, regarding the departure of foreigners from Bosnia and Herzegovina, and regardless of the fact that this was something that the -- that President Izetbegovic personally insisted on, had the Shura not accepted that decision, the detachment would not have been disbanded? Was my -- did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly how it was. That's what happened. In other words, had the people who had sat there and discussed this decided this where everyone was saying, "There's no point in us remaining here, because if we did we would create a conflict with the Bosniaks with whom we fought side by side," we would have -- we would destroy everything that we have accomplished so far, and the authority and respect that we earned would have been destroyed. And our point -- our objective was not to be there to spill the blood of the Muslims but to help them. We did not the Chetniks or the Ustashi. We only went there because they had attacked the Muslims, and we came to assist them with their -- in their resistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 1136, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness -- Mr. Awad, sorry, I just want to be sure about what you ever just told us, because it seems to me that there is a difference in the way the unit was set up and the way it was disbanded. You told us the other day that the detachment had been created because the El Mujahid leadership had asked the 3rd Corps to set up a detachment, and that request was accepted by the 3rd Corps. So the 3rd Corps set up the El Mujahid Detachment, and you told us that this was done in order to regularise the status of the El Mujahid Detachment. So this seems to me to be a willingness to subordinate the El Mujahid Detachment to the army of the -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now -- now you tell us that when then the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina wanted to disband the detachment, then suddenly you would retain your right to maintain the detachment and continue to operate irrespectively of what the Supreme Command or the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina would decide. Now, these two positions seem to me to be in contradiction with each other. So how do you explain the fact you started out by -- by subordinating yourself to the army and then in the end not willing to be disbanded upon the army's order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The detachment would not have been formed had not a decision been made when I said that the Shura -- had the Shura not made the decision to ask for the establishment of the unit for the reasons I mentioned before. I don't need to repeat them again. So the Shura made the decision for us to join the army ranks. Since there was a lot of distrust within the Mujahedin ranks in relation to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina units, because on several occasions -- I'm not going to say that it was treason, but they had been left. They would carry out an attack, and the people who were supposed to go with them forward, they would just leave them. The people were thus exposed and got killed for nothing. They could have stayed alive, but they lost their lives because the people did not support them. So some considered that as treason, and there was a lot of talk about the army's letting us down, others are letting us down. So when you talk about that, not all the people have the same courage. "I don't want to get killed. I want to stay alive. And if there's somebody who can die for me, that's fine. Let the Arabs go, and let them get killed, and I'm going to stay alive." Again, yesterday I clarified that when those loose fighters came, they all got together, the ones who were unaligned, unallied, they sat down with the Shura and made this decision. So it was not a decision for us to have to obey everything, but the decision was that those who are in charge of the army, the army commanders, the unit chain of commanders, were people that we did not have absolute confidence in, absolute trust, because they could betray us. We go out into the field. And I can convey an incident, an event to you, which explains why those people were concerned. They didn't have trust in the commanders of other units. We saw that even during reconnaissance. None of the commanders or those who were important people in those units did not come out into the field to see how their soldiers were carrying out the surveillance, reconnaissance; was the situation really like that on the ground? And sometimes they would just say, "Report back. Everything is good. We're ready," but they didn't actually do the reconnaissance. They didn't know how to plan, for example, a pull-out if necessary. For example, they could be firing, but they would not actually be advancing in certain situations. So because of such circumstances, people had no trust in the commander. And let me tell you sincerely, we only trusted the man whose name was Sakib Mahmuljin as the general of the army, as the commander. We only trusted him, because he was a Muslim and somebody who was sent by the president, the late Alija Izetbegovic, as his man to Zenica. He was the commander. He was the only one we trusted, because he showed us understanding, demonstrated understanding in conversation with us. But we had no confidence or trust at all in the other commanders. And this is why I'm telling you the detachment was formed just for us to be there and to differentiate us from others so that nothing would be ascribed to us. Also, the dismantling of the detachment was something that the people did not accept. It's the end of the war. We cannot force people to wage war. I mean, if I came there to help, I cannot push these people if they don't wish to go there. So we respected the decision of the Bosnian people not to wage any more war, and then we agreed to dismantle the unit. And by Allah had the Shura decided then that the detachment would not be disbanded and that the fighting should continue, nobody could have forced us to dismantle the -- the detachment and to continue fighting. Because we could have entered Zepce in and minute because five people were killed who were very important to us, Sheik Al Rahman, the late Abu Haris, also the late man Abu Zijad [phoen] and some others who were key people in the detachment. So had the Shura not agreed that the detachment be dismantled, nobody would have forced us or could have forced us to dismantle it. The interest of our fighters, us fighters who were fighting there, was to preserve the reputation of those people, to preserve the blood of the Shaheeds. These people did not die in vain. They gave their lives for Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this blood has to be respected. To this very day the people who fought in the El Mujahedin Detachment are ready to get killed and not to kill a single Muslim by their own hand in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So when we say the detachment was formed in a special way, we mean that the Shura brought -- made a decision for it to be formed, and the detachment was dismantled because the Shura had decided to dismantle it, and this is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you would have continued the war if you had so decided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One hundred per cent, 100 per cent. We had weaponry. We had an army. Over 1.500 soldiers were there at the end in the detachment. We had a lot of weapons, materiel, equipment. We could have fought at least three months without cease. But we decided, out of interest -- in the interest of the Bosniak people, because this is what the people had agreed to, they accepted this peace, and we accepted that fighting should be stopped and that the detachment should be dismantled, although the people were in danger when leaving Bosnia and Herzegovina. They even accepted that risk to get killed, to be detained. They accepted that risk, and they left Bosnia and Herzegovina only to -- as a favour to these people here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, thank you for this exhaustive explanation, and I would just like to put one question to you about what you have just said. I heard that you said the Shura made a decision for the El Mujahedin Detachment to join the army, but the decision was not made to obey the army. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how I explained it. People did not trust -- I have to explain again why this was so. People did not trust the Armija commanders. I didn't tell you about some events, and if you wish, I can also tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. What you're saying is very interesting, but there are questions that I still need to put to you, so please -- and our time is limited. Talking yesterday and just now, you, in response to the Prosecutor's questions, you mentioned Sheik Anwar Shaaban. I would now like you to look at a document. It's Exhibit 844.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, it's an article published in the Ljiljan magazine on the 15th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And first all, can you see in front of you the photograph of a person? It's -- is this the late Sheik Enver Shaaban?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would say that this is an interview with Sheik Shaaban. I would like you to turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is also page 2 of the English version, and you can see this on your monitors.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you, please, Witness, to look at the text just below the name of the journalist. It says: "Interview conducted by Nedzad Latic," and then you see the text below where Sheik Enver is introducing himself. He says: "I graduated from the faculty of technical sciences in Cairo, Department for Marine Studies. After that I attended the sharia courses at various faculties. I devoted myself more to the study of the sharia, whether it was in Egypt or abroad." Please, what it says here in this text, is this what you yourself knew about Sheik Enver Shaaban, that he was a very educated person?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Awad, would you accept as correct that that man -- such a man, Enver Shaaban, didn't actually know the grammar of the Arabic language all that well?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever studies Islamic sciences, since that is in Arabic, he had to know grammar. When he quoted or was studying, learning something, or reading a text from that field, he has to use the Arab grammar correctly. He cannot speak slang or street language.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is sufficient. I would now like to ask you something about the Sheik. Sheik Shaaban came to Bosnia in late 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Abu Mali, whom you mentioned several times in your testimony, was actually someone who the Bosnia and Herzegovina army considered as the commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And he had the rank of captain 1st class, or senior captain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now look at D79 -- [Microphone not activated]. And you can put this document away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D7 what?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D790. 790, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, this again is a part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness page 2, paragraphs 190, 191, and 192. 193 also. So can we also scroll the English text down so that the Judges can look at 190, 191, and 192, please, on the screen. Your Honours, the problem is that the English version actually is on two pages. So perhaps we can look at paragraph 190 first from this previous page on the screen. Very well. Maybe it can be arranged in that way, overlapped somehow. Very well. Can we perhaps fit it all on the screen, but Their Honours probably have it in front of them. All right. Maybe we can fold the page. Thank you very much. Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I am sure that you've already read this, this part of the statement. First of all, do you remember that you told the Prosecutor what is said in paragraphs 190, 191, and 192? You -- is it correct, first of all, that you told the Prosecutor what it says here?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. More than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You described that after the Sheik arrived, who knew the Shariat very well, the Arab members of the detachment chose him as the emir, as the man in charge, the leader. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, would you agree with me that the Bosnia and Herzegovina army and their commands did not -- or were not asked or consulted in any way about the election of Sheik Enver as the main leader of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There was no need to ask anyone either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the command of the Bosnia and Herzegovina army did not issue any orders in terms of the Sheik becoming the emir of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the Sheik, as the member of the Egyptian Al Jama Al-Islamiyah, was not accepted by the Saudis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not so. I said -- let me please explain. When there -- it was time to elect the person, Sheik -- the Sheik -- to elect the Sheik, the people who were in the detachment from Saudi Arabia did not accept him for this post because they believed that the late Sheik was a member of the Al Jama Al-Islamiyah, and even -- they even thought that about the other Egyptians. However, they were not members of that particular organisation, so they did not accept our choice for Sheik Enver Shaaban to be the number-one man or the emir of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise. Of I didn't understand all that well, actually, what was written here. I would like to ask you the following: It's correct, isn't it, that precisely because of this matter not -- the Sheik not being accepted by the Saudis as the leader, Abu Mali was actually formally elected as the leader?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, because before Sheik Enver arrived, Dr. Abu Haris was the emir of the El Mujahedin Detachment. But there were misunderstandings between Dr. Abu Haris and certain people in the detachment. They wanted to replace him. With the arrival of Sheik Enver presented this opportunity in the sense that there was a more adequate person than him, because usually the person who leads something that is a religious unit, a religious gathering, the person who knows the Islamic or the religious sciences in the best way is the person that actually leads the group. So this was actually an opportunity for them to replace him. Because of this he couldn't oppose it. There was no ground for that, and there were other people who could take the lead. That's when Sheik Enver Shaaban was elected. But when this happened, when the Saudis did not agree to this, then Abu Haris would no longer accept to be the emir again since this happened. So the solution was found to have Abu Mali as the emir of the El Mujahedin Detachment, but Sheik Enver was still the number-one man. This thing stayed how it was since he was the person who knew the sharia the best.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In other words, Abu Mali was the emir on paper, whereas the real emir of the detachment was Sheik Enver Shaaban; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that -- it was like that. However, the people in the detachment, or most of the people, were not aware of this. Only a part of the Shura who had decided on the replacement, they knew that Sheik Enver was the number-one person, the real emir, and that Abu Mali was the emir in form. So as to avoid any misunderstandings or disagreements within the detachment, Abu Mali was the emir for them. They didn't know about this other decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would suggest the following, and I would ask for you to comment on it: It is true, is it not, that Abu Mali didn't do anything without prior consultation with Sheik Enver?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the Sheik was the real authority in the detachment.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Sheik Enver was a missionary, a dija [phoen]. He was not a fighter, was he?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He focused more on his missionary work than other matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else about Sheik Enver. In your testimony yesterday, you mentioned two meetings of which you said were attended by Sheik Enver and President Izetbegovic. Do you remember mentioning that?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you had a preparatory meeting with the Prosecutor as proofing for your testimony here on the 18th of December, 2007? Do you remember? Do you remember that? Did I give the right date?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't the 18th of December. There were three days. I think the 11th, 12th, and 13th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly you may be right, but I have in mind a letter from the Prosecutor informing the Defence, as he is obliged to do, about certain things from that interview, and what I wish to ask you is the following: You said at the time, among other things, that Sheik Enver discussed with President Izetbegovic problems having to do, among other things, the problem of Bosnian soldiers who had moved from other units to the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you remember discussing this with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that at this meeting there was a discussion with the president to solve the problem of the transfer of members of other units of the BH army to the El Mujahedin Detachment, because there were many fighters who wanted to transfer to the detachment, but their commands, their unit commands, would not approve this transfer. They considered them deserters and sent the military police to detain them. And at this meeting with the late president there was a discussion that this be allowed, and he promised that it would be permitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could you please speak a little more slowly in the interest of the transcript. I wish to ask you now whether you remember when this meeting we are discussing took place, roughly.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the second operation in Zavidovici, which means after the 21st of July, 1995. After the second operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this problem of the transfer of local fighters which the army considered to be deserters was not resolved until this meeting, otherwise it would not have been discussed with President Izetbegovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when talking about this meeting, General Rasim Delic was not present at that meeting, was he?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meeting with the president in Zavidovici in the building of the 35th Division headquarters, army General Rasim Delic was not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were in a position to interpret the Sheik's conversations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a lot but some, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of your own knowledge, did Sheik Enver ever get in touch with Rasim Delic or the Supreme Command Staff regarding the resolution of these problems or any problems regarding the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, except at that meeting, but never before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the meeting that Izetbegovic attended. So as to avoid any confusion, Mr. Awad, when I say "staff," mean the General Staff and General Delic. According to the best of your knowledge, did Sheik Enver ever contact the General Staff and General Delic in connection with this problem?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he did contact Izetbegovic. Is my understanding correct? Asking him to deal with the problem.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did he discuss this with Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command would not allow the transfer of other members of the BH army to the El Mujahedin Detachment, and we asked to have a meeting with the president, because we trust President Alija Izetbegovic. We also trusted General Sakib Mahmuljin. In view of the fact that the commander of the 3rd Corps, General Sakib Mahmuljin, did not accept our request, then we sought somebody we trusted, and that is the late President Alija Izetbegovic in person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you another very simple question. Sheik Enver Shaaban was in no sense subordinated to General Mahmuljin, was he?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't subordinated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more question. Abu Mali, even though he was formally subordinated to the 3rd Corps, did not accept Mahmuljin's orders without the approval of Sheik Enver Shaaban. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this would be a good moment to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Lest I forget, Mr. Awad, can I just check something? Is Sheik -- sorry, Sheik Enver Shaaban and Sheik Anwar Shaaban one and the same person, or are these two different people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is one and the same person. In Arabic you say "Anwar," and the Bosnians say "Enver" for the same name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take break and come back at 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajman -- Awad. Mr. Awad, may we proceed? We were discussing, and you mentioned several times the name of General Sakib Mahmuljin. You said that you trusted him. My question is as follows: When you met him for the first time, who introduced him to you and how? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I met him -- or we met him for the first time in Zenica, at the barracks at Bilmiste. He was introduced by Ahmed Halilovic, saying that this person, Sakib Mahmuljin, had come from Sarajevo and that he was coming on behalf of President Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the talks that you interpreted, for instance between General Mahmuljin and other individuals, was any authorisation given by General Rasim Delic to Mahmuljin ever mentioned, or was he introduced in the way you have just described?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never any mention of Rasim Delic giving any authorisation to him. At that meeting, it was stated that this person, Sakib Mahmuljin, had been sent by President Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I should now like to move on to another topic. With respect to General Mahmuljin, would it be fair to say that your contacts were occasional? They were not permanent or regular?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I say that there were contacts or meetings, it doesn't mean that we met every day. It would occur as necessary, during the operations or something like that. It wasn't on a daily basis. I even remember a period when there were no contacts with him for a period of up to three or four months.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony you mentioned the local commanders several times in whose areas of responsibility you were acting. For instance, General Alagic, Jusuf Musinbegovic [as interpreted]. And my question to you is: These local commanders in whose areas of responsibility you were acting actually wanted to place the detachment under their command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you would not accept that. The El Mujahedin Detachment would not agree to that.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would be formally resubordinated to them, but none of these commanders could give us direct orders. That did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clear that up. When you say that "we were formally resubordinated but no one could give us any orders," which means that there was an order. There was a paper, a piece of paper. However, the detachment did not accept orders from them. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we have a look at an order, P1506. P1506. For the record, Witness, I wish to say that this is an order from the 3rd Corps dated the 28th of August, 1993, whereby the El Mujahedin Detachment, with its entire personnel and materiel is being resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the English version be controlled down -- or up so that Their Honours can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me if I say that at the bottom it says, in handwriting, "Not carried out"? Witness, do you agree that it says here that the entire personnel and technical equipment and materiel shall be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade? My question is: It is true, is it not, that you never in -- were in actual fact resubordinated to that brigade, nor did you is accept their command throughout your stay in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever accept the command of the 330th Brigade and their commander as your commander?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never in our life.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever accept Mr. Jusuf Hasimbegovic [as interpreted] as your commander?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever throughout the fighting in Bosnia and Herzegovina accept the commander of the 7th Brigade as your own commander?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this exhibit into evidence. Could it be assigned a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know whether the witness is able to tell us who signed the note that the order was carried out. The signature on the left of the order that we can see, whose is it? Do you recognise this signature, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 1137, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown Exhibit 439.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, what you said was not translated. Could you please repeat yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked that the witness be shown Exhibit 439, please. E439. For the record, Your Honours, to say that this is the document, this is a document from El Mujahedin Detachment, dated 15 May 1995, entitled "Plan of attack."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to take a look at this document and ask some questions in relation to it. You see that the heading says that this is from the El Mujahedin Detachment. It says there the commander Abu Al Mali. My question would be this: Is it -- it would be correct to say that this plan is in fact the only plan that the detachment forwarded to the BH army. In other words, the detachment did not have a habit of sending its plans to commands of the BH army. Am I correct in saying this?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It was not habitual for the detachment to forward its plans of attacks, from which side the attack would be coming and in what manner it would be carried out. These types of plans were never forwarded. And I think that this document was forwarded, but attack was not carried out, the attack that wasn't carried out in 1994, as a result of which there was great distrust. So in order for us to make them believe us that we are serious in our intent and that we do intend to realise this attack, we sent this plan of attack so that the commander of the 35th Division could be assured that we -- we were doing something, but it wasn't realised, and we -- we didn't know. We couldn't trust such a commander, because we wouldn't know what he would do or what he would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The detachment commander did not forward written reports to the corps or division commands. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It did not send its reports on its personnel, the -- the strength of its unit, for instance, or manpower numbers?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the unit strength, whenever new people came we would change our lists, but this did not happen very often. It didn't happen. It wasn't a daily occurrence. This would happen perhaps once in a month when new people would come and some people would leave. This would be the time where we would enter these changes on the lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to that, I would like to ask you this: You knew that there was a decision issued by General Mahmuljin to ban further admittance of new members into the detachment towards the end of 1994; is that correct? Did you know of this?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall, but I know that there was something to do with replenishment or changes in the numbers and levels of the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it is true, isn't it, that new members were being admitted throughout the period until -- up to the time when the detachment was actually disbanded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have another question. You did not send reports on materiel and technical equipment that you had at your disposal. In other words, what kind of ammunition you had at your disposal or how many weapons. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. We never sent such reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if you don't mind, I just have a little question on this topic. Can I be clear I understand what you are saying, sir. You say this plan of attack was never carried out. In a very short answer, was it ever carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in this manner. Not in the manner that it's -- that is stated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I understand you to be saying that this was yet another fake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, no, no. The attack was carried out, but not in the manner described in this document, because we had assault groups. They had their own plans of attack, the number of people that would participate, along which axis and so on. We did not -- we -- we would say which features would be attacked, but we never stated the manner in which they would be carried out. In other words, the attack was not carried out according to this plan but according to how we wanted to carry it out. And it was carried out, and successfully too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me put my question slightly differently. What then was the purpose of submitting this particular plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as I said a little earlier, because there was such a long lapse of time there was no trust, no confidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A long lapse of time between what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between November 1994 and 27 May 1995. So in this period of time, this is a rather long period of time, nothing happened. Nothing was happening. And because the attack in November was not carried out, the fake attack that I mentioned earlier, there was a sense of distrust. If you recall what I said yesterday, Commander Fadil Hasanagic, when we had the meeting -- okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commander Fadil Hasanagic, the commander of the 35th Division, at a briefing where he said that this attack was not successful, the general was really angry. He was grinding his teeth, and he said, "You are going to stay here with me. You are not going to leave this territory. Don't even think of it. You're staying here." And this is the reason why this sense of distrust creeped in, so that then we wanted to show that we were serious in our intentions to carry out the attack, and in order to accomplish that we provided this plan to show them that something was being done, and that was the only purpose of it. In actual fact, the attack was carried out in our own manner. We decided how we would reach the trenches, what weapons we were going to use, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I would like to ask you something completely different now. Yesterday, in answer to my questions whether the lists that were compiled within the detachment and how they were compiled, you explained that. You were explaining a particular list, if you recall, and now I would like to put some questions in respect of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 663. 663. For the record, this is a document from the 3rd Corps command, dated 7 May 1995, entitled "List," and it is forwarded to the military security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please see page 4 of this document and the name under number 141, 141.

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for Your Honours, I would like to say that this is document that was filed and entered into evidence. Apparently there is no translation of this page, so I would request that the Bosnian version be placed on the ELMO. This is -- to be more precise, this was translated but only the first page, not the list itself. But before we do this, I would just like to see again the first page so that we can see what the headings of -- so that we can -- so that the witness can see the headings of the columns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that the first come up says, "Last and first name," and then "Date of birth," followed by "Place and municipality of birth," and that there is also a column headed "In the army since," followed by "Registered since"? Please bear this in mind while I refer you back to what we were looking at earlier, which is page 4, number 141, where his name is being mentioned. Thank you. Mr. Awad, the name under number 141, would you agree, should be your name?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is the date correct, your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall -- if you recall, the next column where it says 10 September 1992, was -- is supposed to be the column headed "In the army since." Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see that there; right? You see that the date 10 September 1992 is under the heading "In the army since." During your testimony in the past couple of days, you actually said that you arrived in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the end of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me then that this date appearing here, 10 September 1992, as the date of your joining the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And that is why I am having all the problems I'm having with my citizenship now, because it is claimed that I lied to the commission, that I was in the army since this date, whereas I provided different data.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with me, then, that the information contained in this list is not trustworthy, that the date when you joined the army is incorrect, at least in your case?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please remove this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just interrupt you at this stage, Madam Vidovic. We have just received a transcript of the proceedings of the 11th of July, 2007, on which day document PT01462 was admitted into evidence as Exhibit 67. So the record can show that that document has been admitted as Exhibit 67. Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to move to another document. Could the witness please look at Exhibit 97. For the transcript, it's a list of members of the El Mujahedin Detachment of the 26th of February, 1996. I would like the witness to look at page 6 of the document. Before that, before we remove this document, can we please look at 3, page 3, so at that we could look at the column headings. Can we just look at page 3. Your Honours, in the English version this is on page 2 that gives the headings of the columns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the headings. Would you agree that the first one says "Last name, first name," then "Identification number," then "In records since," "Out of unit." "In the records since," and then after that there is a column for "Out of unit." Then there is the information about the municipality of birth, attendance, and see on. Please, can you just remember these columns. . I would now like you to look at page 6 of the document. Page 6 of the document. Can you please look at the name under number 251. 251. Can you please look is that. And here you have "Ajman Awad," and then there are some numbers where the identification number is. Oh, all right. This is very good. Thank you. Then you have "In records since," then you have "Out of the unit." Do you see this information? It says here that you were in the records of the detachment as of the 1st of May, 1993. Yesterday, you told us that you were a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina as of the 13th of August, 1995. 1993. I apologise. 1993. Would you agree with me that this information is not accurate?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that from the moment that the El Mujahedin Detachment was formed, which was part of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, then I was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina as of the 13th of August, 1993.
