utterances.text: Well, let us clarify this a little bit, please. When you were responding just now to the questions of His Honour about killing -- the killing of a humanitarian worker, you said that you and the Shura thus had knowledge that those people were not killers. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This means that the Shura in fact did not have any reason to review that case, because they knew that these people were not killers. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On condition that the Shura knew that these really were killers, could you please tell us if they would have then dealt with this matter?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they should have dealt with that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And something else on that same topic, please. The Judge asked you about legal matters, about adhering to domestic laws. Now I would like to ask you this: You recall me showing you a document a little bit earlier from which it can be clearly concluded that pursuant to the Bosnia and Herzegovina laws foreigners should have, must have, given statements on voluntary membership of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say that that is the law, then that is the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You saw that in the document. The document referred to the duty of providing a statement to that effect about joining -- about a foreign volunteer voluntarily joining the army. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you accept that you did not obey that particular law? It was not applied. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In other words, do you accept that you did not consider it your duty to apply the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina which did not coincide with some of your convictions about conduct or some of your rules?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Awad, I just wanted to put one more question to you which arises from the questions put to you by Her Honour Judge Lattanzi, and it has to do with this organisation, the Mowafaq organisation. I would like to ask you this: Was the seat of the organisation in Saudi Arabia?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was Saudi Arabia. I know that the foundation was registered in Zagreb. It's possible that their seat was in Saudi Arabia. Possibly it was in the United States. I'm not sure where the seat was. It's something that I did not really think about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know that Jasin Abdulah Al Kaidi [phoen] was for a while at the head of this organisation? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jasin Al Kaidi perhaps was the founder or the owner. In any case, I did hear of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Have you also heard about Kiafiq bin Muhammed Aijaidi [phoen] as at the head of the organisation?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is Shafik Al Aiad [phoen]. Shafik al Aiad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is that a person linked to the organisation?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my director.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Can you please tell me if -- well, you mentioned that the organisation was registered in Zagreb. Please, is it correct that the organisation - I'm talking about the Mowafaq Foundation - was connected with the Croatian Islamic Centre, if you know?

utterances.speaker: AIMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked for them very briefly. I was in Zagreb for 15 days only working for that organisation, so I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Awad, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Awad, there's -- that brings us to the conclusion of your testimony, and let me take this opportunity to give you our heart-felt thanks as the Chamber for coming to testify, and we know that we -- it's been quite a strenuous couple of days -- three days. It was not easy, but we are happy that you could stay on have the staying power to the end. Thank you very much, and best of luck in your future endeavours. You are now excused. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having the time to what are me. I like to talk a lot, and thank you for your patience in listening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We really appreciate it. You are excused. You may stand down. Thank you very much. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then obviously today you given off for tomorrow morning. We'll go home. Thank you very much. Will the court -- court adjourned. Do we adjourn to a specific date? I thought there was a tentative arrangement for the 14th. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I do believe we're on the court's schedule for the 14th. I believe that's in the afternoon, for purposes of the 98 bis proceedings. I think prior to that I should officially indicate that the Prosecution rests. We've closed our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I'll put that on the record. And it's my understanding that we'll have the 98 bis proceeding in the afternoon on Thursday, the 14th of February. That's -- that's certainly my understanding at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar has just indicated that it will be in Courtroom II. In the ICTY, not at the state court. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Nothing else from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in that event, then, maybe what remains to be done is once again to place on record our thanks to the state court of the BiH for receiving us and giving us the use of their facilities and for the very kind treatment they extended to us during our stay here. I guess it is not inappropriate to mention that the meals have very good, and the staff has very been very kind to us. Everybody has been very helpful. And over and above whatever thanks will be given, we just wanted to record this to the President of the court and to ask her to extend our thanks to the rest of her staff. Thank you very much. Court adjourned to the 14th of February, Courtroom II, ICTY, at 2.15. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of February, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
